introduction: Starting a venture is one of the best ways to learn how all the parts of a business fit together. In this project-based course, student teams find a real customer problem, test whether people care about it, and build a venture plan around the solution. Building on Design Thinking Studio (BBA206), Marketing Management (BBA301) and Financial Management (BBA302), the course takes teams through opportunity identification, customer discovery, business models, minimum viable products, unit economics, funding and the legal basics of starting up in India. Progress is reviewed at fixed milestones, and each team closes with a final report and viva. The course prepares students for the Capstone Consulting Project (BBA603).
plagiarism: Plagiarism above 15% (checked by software) in any submission, or any use of unauthorised AI tools in exams, leads to zero marks for that component. Repeat cases go to the Academic Integrity Committee, chaired by the Dean.

objectives.text: To introduce the entrepreneurial mindset and the Indian start-up ecosystem.
To develop skill in finding opportunities and testing them with real customers.
To enable students to build a complete and financially sound venture plan.
To develop confidence in pitching a venture to mentors and investors.

textbooks.text: Barringer, Bruce R. and Ireland, R. Duane. Entrepreneurship: Successfully Launching New Ventures. Pearson. (latest edition; to be confirmed by faculty)

readings.text: Ries, Eric. The Lean Startup. Crown Business.
Osterwalder, Alexander and Pigneur, Yves. Business Model Generation. Wiley.
Blank, Steve and Dorf, Bob. The Startup Owner's Manual. Wiley.

clos.text: Apply core entrepreneurship concepts to identify and describe a viable venture opportunity.
clos.plg_label: PLG 1: Understanding and Application of Fundamentals
clos.exceed: Describes a specific, well-researched opportunity and applies entrepreneurship concepts accurately and with insight.
clos.meet: Describes a clear opportunity and applies the main concepts correctly.
clos.below: The opportunity is vague or unsupported, or concepts are misapplied.
clos.analysis: 85.0% of students met or exceeded expectations against a target of 70%, and 15.0% did not meet them. The class averaged 67.5% on this CLO. It was assessed through Venture Proposal.
clos.improvement: Keep the current approach, and raise the Bloom's level of Venture Proposal so the CLO is tested in more depth.

clos.text: Identify a real customer problem and validate a solution using primary research and data.
clos.mode: Milestone Reviews: evidence from customer interviews and MVP tests (Mentor Assessment as a supporting measure)
clos.exceed: Gathers strong evidence from real customers, changes direction when the data demands it, and shows a validated solution.
clos.meet: Gathers enough customer evidence to confirm the problem and tests a solution at least once.
clos.below: Relies on assumptions rather than customer evidence, or ignores what the evidence shows.
clos.analysis: 87.5% of students met or exceeded expectations against a target of 70%, and 12.5% did not meet them. The class averaged 64.3% on this CLO. It was assessed through Milestone Reviews.
clos.improvement: Keep the current approach, and add a stretch task for students who already exceed expectations.

clos.text: Build an integrated venture plan that links market, operations, finance and the external environment.
clos.mode: Final Report and Viva: written venture plan
clos.exceed: All parts of the plan fit together, financial projections follow from stated assumptions, and external risks are critically assessed.
clos.meet: The plan covers all functional areas with reasonable projections and notes the main external risks.
clos.below: Parts of the plan contradict each other, projections are unsupported, or external factors are ignored.
clos.analysis: 67.5% of students met or exceeded expectations against a target of 70%, and 32.5% did not meet them. The class averaged 56.7% on this CLO. It was assessed through Final Written Plan.
clos.improvement: Add two graded practice cases on Final Written Plan before the assessment, with a worked model answer and the rubric shared in advance.

clos.text: Pitch a venture persuasively in writing and in person.
clos.mode: Final Report and Viva: team pitch and viva
clos.exceed: Delivers a compelling, well-structured pitch and handles tough questions with clear, evidence-based answers.
clos.meet: Delivers a clear pitch and answers most questions adequately.
clos.below: The pitch is unclear or unconvincing, or the team cannot defend its plan.
clos.analysis: 82.5% of students met or exceeded expectations against a target of 70%, and 17.5% did not meet them. The class averaged 62.0% on this CLO. It was assessed through Pitch and Viva.
clos.improvement: Add a revision session on Pitch and Viva before the assessment.
